facts.text: Rochester Hills is a city in Oakland County that was Avon Township until November 20, 1984, and it is separate from the City of Rochester, which borders part of its east side.

Rochester Hills is bordered by Oakland Charter Township to the north, Troy to the south along South Boulevard, Shelby Township in Macomb County to the east along Dequindre Road, and Auburn Hills to the west.
Early settlers found heavily wooded, gently rolling land crossed by rivers and creeks, and the area's first mills ran on waterpower from the Clinton River, Stony Creek and Paint Creek.

After 1900, many Avon Township farms were sold for housing subdivisions, scientific farming operations and large country estates, and by 1950 the former farm community had become a suburb whose families earned their livelihoods elsewhere.
The Clinton River Trail, a multi-use trail on 16 miles of abandoned rail line through Sylvan Lake, Pontiac, Auburn Hills, Rochester Hills and Rochester, runs 4.5 miles through Rochester Hills.
Innovation Hills park on West Hamlin Road sits along the Clinton River, with ponds, a waterfall, a paved and boardwalk trail and a nature-themed playground.
The Rochester Hills Museum at Van Hoosen Farm sits on rolling park grounds bordered by Stoney Creek, with a large grove of mature black walnut and maple trees around its gazebo.
The city has two main historic districts, Stoney Creek and Winkler Mill, plus a number of stand-alone historic properties.
Rochester Hills hosts college and graduate programs at Oakland University and Rochester Christian University.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Rochester Hills, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas light installation in Rochester Hills, MI for homes on wooded, rolling lots: rooflines, tree wraps, shrubs and takedown. Free estimate.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Rochester Hills, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Lighting for Rochester Hills rooflines, trees and shrubs, designed for wooded, rolling lots, with takedown handled after the season.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Early settlers found Rochester Hills heavily wooded and gently rolling, and long after the farms gave way to subdivisions and estates, a lot can still carry that character in mature trees and changes in grade. Terrain shapes holiday lighting more than people expect. A yard that slopes toward the street changes how the roofline reads from the road, and a stand of mature trees can frame the house or hide it. We walk the property, note grade, trees and power, and design a display that looks balanced from where neighbors and guests actually see it. Where the ground lets a bucket truck set up, it lifts the crew to tall trees and high peaks, and the lights come down after the holidays as part of the job.
considerations: Rolling yards affect where ladders stand and where the lift can park. We check grade and ground conditions during the estimate, so installation day starts with a plan for every run instead of improvising on a hillside in November.

On a wooded lot, the house may be seen through trunks rather than across open lawn. Wrapping the nearest trees and lighting the entry pulls the eye toward the house, while the roofline gives it a clean top edge. We balance all three in the design.

Evergreens keep their shape all winter and can be wrapped or draped for a full look. Bare hardwoods show off trunk and branch wraps instead. On a mixed lot, we choose which trees carry the display so the yard looks designed rather than scattered.
faq: Do you serve Rochester Hills and the City of Rochester?

Yes, Rochester Hills is within the area we serve. The City of Rochester, which borders part of Rochester Hills on the east, is a separate city right next door, so include your full address when you ask for an estimate, and we will confirm coverage for that address.
Our subdivision has an HOA. Do we need approval?

It depends on your association's rules. Some boards review exterior decorations or set dates for when displays can go up and come down. Check with your board early; a written estimate with the layout in it gives them something concrete to approve.

Holiday installs generally fill October, November and the first days of December, and takedown follows the holidays. Booking early gives you more say in the install date, which matters on larger wooded lots that take more planning. Calls later in the fall are welcome too.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Rochester Hills, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Subdivision entrance and commercial holiday lighting in Rochester Hills, MI, with board-ready plans for HOAs, businesses and managers. Free estimate.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Rochester Hills, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Subdivision entrances, business frontages and office properties lit for the season, with one contact from walkthrough to removal.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: After 1900, many of the area's farms were sold for housing subdivisions, and today a subdivision entrance, with its sign, planted island and trees, is often the first thing drivers see. A lit entrance tells residents and visitors the neighborhood is cared for, and entrance lighting is a core part of our commercial work. The same approach carries to businesses, offices and managed properties across the city: design for how people arrive, install cleanly with bucket trucks where height calls for it, service the display through the season and remove it afterward. Boards and managers get a written plan that is easy to review and approve.
considerations: Power at a subdivision entrance is often limited, sometimes a single outlet near the sign. The walkthrough locates every outlet and circuit before design begins, so the plan fits what the entrance can actually run rather than what looks good on paper.

HOA boards need something clear to vote on. The estimate lays out what gets lit, how it will look and what the season includes, from installation through removal, so the board can decide at one meeting instead of trading emails for weeks.

For businesses and offices, lighting that frames the entrance, wraps landscape trees and outlines the roofline makes a property read as open and active in December. Install and takedown dates are set around your business hours, parking and deliveries.
faq: Do you light subdivision entrances in Rochester Hills?

Yes. Associations in Rochester Hills can schedule a site visit at the entrance at no charge, estimate included. Typical elements include sign lighting, wrapped trees, lit shrubs and lamppost decor, all planned around the power available at the entrance.
Can one plan cover several entrances?

Neighborhoods with more than one entrance, and property managers who look after several associations or buildings, can get one coordinated design and one estimate. That keeps the look consistent and gives you one contact for service and removal.
Can the entrance lighting match our neighborhood's style?

Of course. Some associations want classic warm white, others want color or a look tied to the entrance sign. We sketch options during the walkthrough, design around the sign, plantings and trees already at the entrance, then put the plan in writing for the board.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Roofline Lighting in Rochester Hills, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Permanent roofline lighting in Rochester Hills, MI, planned for wooded, rolling lots and controlled by app all year. Get a free estimate.
permanent-lighting.h1: Permanent Lighting in Rochester Hills, MI
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: A permanent roofline outline you control from your phone, planned to show through the trees on a wooded lot.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: On a wooded Rochester Hills lot, a house can go quiet behind the trees once the sun sets. Permanent lighting gives it a clear outline every evening. The track itself hugs the roofline beneath the eaves and blends in by day. Colors, scenes and schedules come from the app: warm white or classic multicolor for the holidays, a bright scene for a backyard party and a soft accent outline on ordinary nights. On rolling ground, where a house may sit above or below the street, we plan the runs so the outline reads evenly from the road. Installation happens once, and we walk through the app with you before leaving.
considerations: Permanent lighting becomes part of the house. If your subdivision's association reviews exterior changes, or the home sits in the Stoney Creek or Winkler Mill historic district, find out what approval is needed before you schedule. Share the estimate with them; it lists the track placement and hardware.

Rolling ground means some houses sit above the road and others below it. We check sight lines from the street and the drive, then plan the track so the outline stays even and continuous from the angles people actually see.

Permanent lights draw from a power source near the roofline, often in the garage. On a larger home with several wings, we plan where power feeds in and how runs join, so the joints stay hidden and the wiring stays neat.
faq: Do you offer permanent lighting across Rochester Hills?

Yes, for homes throughout the city. Put your address on the estimate request; the visit covers your roofline, the power supply and, on a wooded lot, which trees stand close to the house. A layout follows, along with a written estimate listing what the job covers.
Can we switch to team colors for game day?

Easily. Set team colors before kickoff and switch back to warm white afterward, or schedule the change ahead of time for the whole season. The same app handles holiday scenes, birthdays and a simple nightly accent.
Can we still add seasonal lights?

You can. A permanent roofline pairs well with seasonal tree wraps or shrub lighting for December. Among the trees, that combination gives both a clean outline and depth in the yard, and both can go on the same estimate.
